leads.posting: AI video platform Clueso raises $10 Mn in Series A round led by Dharana Capital. AI video platform Clueso has raised $10 million in a Series A funding round led by Dharana Capital, with participation from new investors Founders Future and Neotribe Ventures. Existing investors Y Combinator and f7 Ventures also participated in the round. The latest funding takes the company’s total capital raised to $12 million. According to the company, more than 80% of the Series A capital came from existing investors. Founded by Akash Anand, Prajwal Prakash and Neel Balar, Clueso provides an AI-powered platform that helps businesses create and update videos for marketing, customer education, onboarding, training and internal operations. The company said its platform is used by more than 1,000 businesses, including Atlassian, Zendesk, Gainsight, Seismic and Ironclad. According to Clueso, its customers have reported more than fivefold productivity gains and an 80% reduction in video production costs. Clueso uses AI agents to automate different stages of video production, including capturing software workflows, generating scripts and voiceovers, editing footage and maintaining brand consistency. The platform can also update videos when products or business processes change. The company also offers integrations with other business tools and support for the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which allows AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT to create, edit and manage videos through Clueso. Clueso said it will use the fresh capital to expand its enterprise sales and go-to-market operations, develop its AI agent capabilities, improve editing features and strengthen integrations with business software. The funding comes amid growing adoption of AI tools across enterprise workflows, including content creation, employee training and customer education. leads.posting: GreenCell Mobility Raises ₹330 Cr To Expand Electric Bus Fleet. Everstone Capital-backed EV startup GreenCell Mobility has raised ₹330 Cr ($34.6 Mn) in an equity funding round led by Impact Fund Denmark to support the rollout of about 4,500 electric buses currently under deployment. The Mumbai-based startup is eyeing expanding its fleet to more than 5,000 e-buses across 105 cities across India. “Our focus is on executing our order book with rigour, strengthening service delivery and ensuring that the organisation keeps pace with the size and complexity of our operations. This equity investment gives us greater headroom to accelerate our plans while maintaining the standards of reliability, efficiency and customer experience that are fundamental to our business,” GreenCell Mobility managing director and chief executive Devndra Chawla said. Founded in 2019, GreenCell Mobility focuses on deploying and operating electric buses for public transportation. It acquires electric buses via contract manufacturing arrangements with vendors and then deploys them for both intercity and intracity travel. Backed by Eversource Capital, a joint venture between Everstone Capital and Lightsource, GreenCell primarily operates under the brand NueGo. It claims to operate more than 1,200 electric buses in India, including 900 on intra-city routes, 300 under its NueGo brand for inter-city travel, and 50 for MSRTC. The startup also runs over 270 charging stations to support its fleet. The startup previously raised $37 Mn from World Bank’s International Finance Corporation and also counts Eversource Capital, British International Investment and Tata Capital among its backers. India’s electric bus segment has so far drawn strong interest from development finance institutions and lenders backing vehicle deployments under long-term public transport contracts. leads.posting: ThinkMetal raises Rs 27 Cr led by IAN Alpha Fund. Advanced materials and manufacturing startup ThinkMetal has raised Rs 27 crore in a funding round led by IAN Alpha Fund, with participation from 3i Partners and existing investors. The proceeds will be used to develop its products, expand its research and development capabilities, and increase adoption among industrial customers. Founded by Sabyasachi Ghosh and Arushi Sharma, ThinkMetal is developing indigenous technologies for precision metal manufacturing. Its platform combines advanced materials, manufacturing processes and industrial systems to reduce production time and dependence on imported technologies. The company’s current commercial offering is SistemT1, a metal additive manufacturing system designed to produce precision metal components. The system uses ThinkMetal’s proprietary FuseX metal filament technology. The company is also expanding its materials library and developing in-house capabilities to process new materials. ThinkMetal serves manufacturers across aerospace, defence, space, automotive and electric mobility. It has moved from technology development to enterprise pilots and is now working towards larger commercial deployments. According to IAN Alpha Fund, the company has filed more than 17 intellectual property applications. The company claims its technology can manufacture high-value precision metal parts up to 10 times faster and at half the cost of conventional methods.

leads.posting: Bharat Digital Anywhere The Build for Bharat Fellowship is a paid, six-month programme that places early-career engineers, designers and AI practitioners inside government departments. Fellows work alongside government teams on real projects, improving public systems used by millions of people. What fellows get: Real-world experience: Work on live government projects, interact with users and understand how public services operate. Learning and mentorship: An orientation, regular reviews and expert office hours with practitioners such as Kailash Nadh (CTO, Zerodha), Rukmini S (Founder, Data for India) and Devanshi Sihare (TinkerLabs). A community: Learn alongside other fellows and connect with people working in public technology. Some projects from past cohorts Official statistics: Built MoSPI’s eSankhyiki MCP server , making official statistics accessible to AI assistants. Rural libraries: Developed Arivu Mitra, a WhatsApp companion for Gram Panchayat librarians in Karnataka using Whatomate . Transport: Built a transit analytics dashboard for Chennai’s transport authority and NHAI's Annual Pass web and app which has helped sell 1 Cr Annual Passes in a year. Citizen services: Redesigned Tamil Nadu’s e-Sevai services, IRCTC ticket UI, e-swathu, etc., to improve the citizen experience. Explore more projects Fellowship at a glance Duration : January–June 2027 (6 months, on-site) Location: On-site at a partner government department Stipend: ₹40,000 per month Eligibility: Indian citizens graduating in 2027 or who completed their latest degree in 2024–2026, with demonstrable skills in Engineering, Design or AI Application deadline: 18 October 2026, 11:59 PM IST Apply here: https://bharatdigital.org/fellowship

Apply now Best viewed on Desktop × Home Fellowship Build for Bharat Fellowship 2027 Past Cohorts Past Projects About Get Involved Build for Bharat Fellowship 2027 A six-month paid fellowship inside a government department, working alongside government partners, solving tasks for real-world impact. Apply for 2027 cohort Read the FAQs We aim to identify and train early-career public-interest technologists who can strengthen, modernise and humanise the digital systems solving India's most urgent public and governance challenges. What the fellowship holds 01 Orientation and onboarding Before you start, an orientation in public service, policy and what it takes to put technology inside complex social systems. You hear from some of India’s top technologists, policymakers, designers and administrators. Much of it is tacit knowledge you won’t find anywhere else, there to ready you for the six months ahead. Watch last year’s orientation ↗ The 2026 cohort 02 Build Once deputed to a government team, you work alongside the people already there, on real problems and real codebases. Most fellows ship changes to government systems within their first month, and a few go on to redesign or launch services used by millions of Indians. This is the real thing, not a hackathon or a side-project. A session with an anganwadi group · RDPR Karnataka 03 Mentorship Throughout the fellowship, you have regular mentoring and check-ins with Bharat Digital’s core team. On top of that, you get office hours with some of India’s leading public-spirited technologists and designers. Previous mentors include Kailash Nadh (CTO, Zerodha), Rukmini S (Data for India; author of Whole Numbers and Half Truths ) and Devanshi Sihare (Head of Social Impact, TinkerLabs). Fellows with mentor Rukmini S · Data for India 04 Field visits Field visits are an integral part of the fellowship. Not a line of code gets changed until you’ve understood the problem first-hand: visited the offices and rooms where your technology will be used, and met the people it will affect. By the end, you won’t just have immersed yourself in India’s grassroots; you’ll understand how public systems are actually conceived, and how they touch the ground. StoryWeaver Lite with children in a Gram Panchayat library · RDPR Karnataka 05 Community building We believe deeply in the power of community. We create opportunities for fellows to get to know one another across cohorts, and to plug into the wider public-technology ecosystem through events, talks and one-on-one sessions with founders and practitioners. A mixer for the 2025 and 2026 cohorts 06 Public technology careers Six months inside a department changes what you can do next, and often what you want to do next. We work closely with you to find that next step, so you can keep building in the public-technology ecosystem: in government, in research labs, or at the leading tech-for-good organisations using technology to improve public systems.
